info.name: auth-service
info.description:
auth-service (Play, Java): nginx /auth/** -> gateway (public) -> auth-service.

- `POST /auth/login` with `{"email", "password"}` returns `{access_token, token_type: "Bearer", expires_in: 600}`. The JWT is HS256-signed and carries the `email` claim; it is valid for 10 minutes.
- `POST /auth/signup` with `{"email", "password"}` (password 8-72 bytes) returns `201 {id, email, createdAt}`, or `409` if the email is already registered.

- `POST /auth/password-reset/request` `{"email"}` always returns `202`; if the account exists, a one-time token (valid 15 minutes) is emailed. `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` `{"token", "newPassword"}` returns `204`.
- `POST /auth/password/change` (JWT required) `{"currentPassword", "newPassword"}` returns `204`.

Set `userEmail` / `userPassword` (defaults: the seed user from `.env`). **Login - success** stores the token in `accessToken`. **Using the token** shows how the gateway treats tokens. **Sign up**, **Forgot password** and **Change password** each create a new, uniquely named user on every run (they are not deleted), so the seed user's password is never changed. The password folders read emails from Mailpit (`/mailpit/api/v1/...`) and retry for a few seconds when run in the Collection Runner or newman.

exec: pm.test('email claim is the logged-in user', () => pm.expect(claims.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('userEmail').toLowerCase()));
pm.test('Valid for exactly 10 minutes', () => pm.expect(claims.exp - claims.iat).to.eql(600));
pm.test('email claim is normalised to lower case', () => pm.expect(jwtPart(pm.response.json().access_token, 1).email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('userEmail').toLowerCase()));
